test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated user is redirected from the Project Statuses page
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Project Statuses page URL without being logged in.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user with view access can see the statuses and their sub-statuses
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with view access.
2. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses.
test_cases.expected: The page loads and displays all main project statuses grouped with their associated sub-statuses. No Add, Edit, Toggle, or Delete actions are visible.

test_cases.scenario: Add Sub-Status button is visible in the page header
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses.
test_cases.expected: An 'Add Sub-Status' button is visible in the page header along with Import and Export buttons.

test_cases.scenario: Main project statuses cannot be created, edited, or deleted by users
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses.
2. Look for any way to add, edit, or delete a main status (e.g., 'In Progress', 'Completed').
test_cases.expected: No actions are available to create, modify, or remove main statuses. They are system-defined and fixed. Only sub-statuses can be managed.

test_cases.scenario: Project Statuses page loads with a grouped layout showing main statuses and their sub-statuses
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses.
test_cases.expected: The page shows the 'Projects / Configurations' eyebrow, 'Project Statuses' heading, and subtitle 'Manage project statuses and their sub-statuses across your organisation.' After a loading spinner, the content area shows main statuses grouped with their sub-statuses listed beneath each.

test_cases.scenario: Loading spinner is shown while the status list loads
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses and observe the page while it loads.
test_cases.expected: A loading spinner is briefly visible before the status groups appear.

test_cases.scenario: Each main status section displays its associated sub-statuses
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses.
2. View each main status group.
test_cases.expected: Each main status (e.g., 'Not Started', 'In Progress', 'Completed') shows its list of sub-statuses beneath it. If a main status has no sub-statuses, the section is still visible with an empty or 'no sub-statuses' indicator.

test_cases.scenario: Sub-statuses show their active/inactive status
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses.
2. Look at the sub-statuses within a main status group.
test_cases.expected: Each sub-status indicates whether it is active or inactive (e.g., via a badge or status indicator).

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Add Sub-Status opens the create sub-status drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses.
2. Click 'Add Sub-Status' in the page header.
test_cases.expected: The create sub-status drawer slides open with a Main Status dropdown and a Sub-Status Name field.

test_cases.scenario: Creating a sub-status with valid details adds it under the selected main status
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create sub-status drawer.
2. Select a main status from the dropdown (e.g., 'In Progress').
3. Enter a sub-status name (e.g., 'Draft').
4. Click 'Add Sub-Status'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. The new sub-status 'Draft' appears under the 'In Progress' main status group on the page.

test_cases.scenario: Main Status is required — cannot create a sub-status without selecting one
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create sub-status drawer.
2. Leave the Main Status field unselected.
3. Enter a sub-status name.
4. Click 'Add Sub-Status'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the Main Status field. The sub-status is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Sub-Status Name is required — cannot create without it
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create sub-status drawer.
2. Select a main status but leave the Sub-Status Name blank.
3. Click 'Add Sub-Status'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the Sub-Status Name field. The sub-status is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Sub-Status Name has a maximum length of 100 characters
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create sub-status drawer.
2. Enter more than 100 characters in the Sub-Status Name field.
test_cases.expected: The character counter updates as the user types. The field enforces the 100-character limit.

test_cases.scenario: Character counter shows remaining characters for the Sub-Status Name
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create sub-status drawer.
2. Type into the Sub-Status Name field.
test_cases.expected: A character counter updates in real time (e.g., '5 / 100').

test_cases.scenario: Cancel button closes the create sub-status drawer without saving
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create sub-status drawer.
2. Enter some details.
3. Click 'Cancel'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No sub-status is created.

test_cases.scenario: Duplicate sub-status name under the same main status is rejected
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create sub-status drawer.
2. Select a main status.
3. Enter a sub-status name that already exists under that main status.
4. Click 'Add Sub-Status'.
test_cases.expected: An error appears indicating the sub-status name already exists for that main status.

test_cases.scenario: Edit action opens the edit sub-status drawer pre-populated with the current name
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Edit action on a sub-status.
(The Edit action may appear in a row action within each main status section.)
test_cases.expected: The edit sub-status drawer opens. The Main Status field shows the parent status as read-only (view-field). The Sub-Status Name field is pre-populated with the current name.

test_cases.scenario: Main Status cannot be changed in the edit drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a sub-status.
2. Attempt to change the Main Status field.
test_cases.expected: The Main Status field is read-only (shown as a view-field, not an editable dropdown). The parent status cannot be changed after creation.

test_cases.scenario: Saving changes updates the sub-status name
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a sub-status.
2. Change the Sub-Status Name.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. The sub-status shows the updated name in the list.

test_cases.scenario: Sub-Status Name cannot be cleared in edit
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a sub-status.
2. Clear the Sub-Status Name field.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears. The change is not saved.

test_cases.scenario: Cancel button in the edit drawer discards changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a sub-status.
2. Change the name.
3. Click 'Cancel'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The sub-status name is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Character counter updates in the edit drawer as the user types
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Edit the Sub-Status Name field.
test_cases.expected: The character counter updates in real time.

test_cases.scenario: Toggle action on an active sub-status opens a deactivation confirmation
test_cases.steps:
1. Find an active sub-status.
2. Click its Toggle action.
test_cases.expected: A deactivation confirmation modal appears.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deactivation sets the sub-status to Inactive
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle on an active sub-status.
2. Confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. A success toast appears. The sub-status shows as Inactive in its section.

test_cases.scenario: Toggle action on an inactive sub-status opens an activation confirmation
test_cases.steps:
1. Find an inactive sub-status.
2. Click its Toggle action.
test_cases.expected: An activation confirmation modal appears.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming activation sets the sub-status to Active
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle on an inactive sub-status.
2. Confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The sub-status shows as Active in its section.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the toggle confirmation makes no change
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle on a sub-status.
2. Click Cancel in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The sub-status status is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Delete action opens a confirmation modal
test_cases.steps: 1. Click Delete on a sub-status.
test_cases.expected: A delete confirmation modal appears with the sub-status name.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deletion removes the sub-status from its main status section
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a sub-status.
2. Confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. A success toast appears. The sub-status is removed from the page.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling deletion makes no changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a sub-status.
2. Click Cancel in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The sub-status remains in the list.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Import opens the import panel for sub-statuses
test_cases.steps: 1. Click 'Import' in the page header.
test_cases.expected: The import view opens allowing a file to be uploaded for importing sub-statuses.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Export opens the export panel
test_cases.steps: 1. Click 'Export' in the page header.
test_cases.expected: The export panel opens, allowing sub-statuses to be exported.

test_cases.scenario: Export file contains sub-status data including the associated main status
test_cases.steps: 1. Click Export and download the file.
test_cases.expected: The exported file includes sub-status names and their associated main status labels.

test_cases.scenario: Page refreshes to show newly imported sub-statuses after import completes
test_cases.steps:
1. Import a valid sub-statuses file.
2. Complete the import.
test_cases.expected: The statuses container refreshes. Newly imported sub-statuses appear under their respective main status groups.

test_cases.scenario: Project Statuses page loads within an acceptable time
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses.
test_cases.expected: The loading spinner is brief. The grouped status list renders within 3 seconds.

test_cases.scenario: Session expiry during an action redirects to login
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create sub-status drawer.
2. Let the session expire.
3. Attempt to save.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page. No data is saved.

test_cases.scenario: Status groups update after creating or deleting a sub-status
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a sub-status under a main status.
2. Observe the page after the drawer closes.
test_cases.expected: The sub-status appears in the appropriate main status group without a full page reload.

test_cases.scenario: Status groups and sub-statuses are clearly laid out on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: Each main status is shown as a distinct section with its sub-statuses listed beneath it. The layout is clear and readable without horizontal scrolling.

test_cases.scenario: Add Sub-Status, Import, and Export buttons are all visible in the page header on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Project Statuses page on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: All three header buttons are visible in the top-right area.

test_cases.scenario: Status groups and sub-statuses are readable on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Open Projects / Configurations > Project Statuses on a mobile device.
test_cases.expected: The status groups and their sub-statuses stack vertically and are readable without horizontal scrolling. No content is clipped.

test_cases.scenario: Create sub-status drawer is usable on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Tap 'Add Sub-Status' on a mobile device.
test_cases.expected: The create sub-status drawer opens in a mobile-friendly layout. The Main Status dropdown and Sub-Status Name field are easy to interact with.

test_cases.scenario: Sub-status actions are accessible on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. On a mobile device, view a sub-status row and look for its actions (Edit, Toggle, Delete).
test_cases.expected: Actions are accessible via a tap or overflow menu on mobile.

test_cases.scenario: Newly created sub-status appears in the project status dropdown when editing a project
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a sub-status under the 'In Progress' main status.
2. Navigate to a project and open the status field.
3. Select 'In Progress' as the main status and look for available sub-statuses.
test_cases.expected: The newly created sub-status is available for selection under 'In Progress' on the project.

test_cases.scenario: Deactivating a sub-status removes it from available sub-status selections in projects
test_cases.steps:
1. Deactivate a sub-status.
2. Try to assign that sub-status to a project.
test_cases.expected: The deactivated sub-status no longer appears in the sub-status selection for projects.

test_cases.scenario: Projects with a deleted sub-status retain a reference to the former sub-status or show a graceful fallback
test_cases.steps:
1. Delete a sub-status that is currently assigned to one or more projects.
2. View one of those projects.
test_cases.expected: The project either retains the deleted sub-status name for historical display, or shows a clear indicator that the sub-status no longer exists. No error or blank field appears unexpectedly.
